model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Gottheimer: a slightly Democratic district, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage of more than $13 million to his challenger's $9,000, with both major prediction markets pricing his win odds near 96%. With no polling to contradict these signals, the race stays in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A sharp national shift against Democrats or a late wave of outside spending against Gottheimer could narrow the margin, though no such spending is currently in the district.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Gottheimer, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election with an enormous financial edge: more than $13 million in cash on hand after raising $5.5 million, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised under $100,000 and reports roughly $9,000 available. Betting markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Gottheimer's chances at about 96 percent, and no outside groups have committed serious spending to the district.

The district leans slightly Democratic, and the incumbent's personal brand has historically run ahead of the partisan baseline here. With no public general-election polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which point the same direction. Kirrane would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or a late infusion of outside money to become competitive; as it stands, Gottheimer is a heavy favorite to win another term.
